TWO MORE BOOKS NAMING KANAWANA, both lending-restricted on the Internet Archive and neither
readable from here. Each passage assembled 2026-09-06 from overlapping Open Library
search-inside windows. RECONSTRUCTIONS, not transcriptions.

================================================================================
1. Stuart McLean, "The Vinyl Cafe Notebooks" (Toronto: Viking Canada, 2010)
   Internet Archive item vinylcafenoteboo0000mcle, scan leaf 378.

QUERIES: "Kanawana" "Sir George Williams" ; "Kamp Kanawana on the shores of Lake Kanawana" ;
         "Kanawana is where" ; "where I found my sea legs" ; "1969, 1 got a job at Kamp" ;
         "began for me. In the summer of" Kanawana ; "where I was able to leave the" ;
         "shaky and uncertain turbulence" ; "of my adolescence behind and" ;
         "find the road, or, more to the"

RECONSTRUCTED (the OCR reads "1 got" for "I got"):

  ... [Kanawana is] where it all began for me. In the summer of 1969, [I] got a job at Kamp
  Kanawana on the shores of Lake Kanawana in the Laurentian Mountains. Kanawana is where I found
  my sea legs, where I was able to leave the shaky and uncertain turbulence of my adolescence
  behind and find the road, or, more to the point, find the where[-]withal ...

The bracketed opening is supplied: the first window begins at "where it all began for me" and
the subject before it was not recovered. The sentence after "wherewithal" was not recovered
either. The same leaf carries McLean on Sir George Williams University, which is how the passage
was found — a query pairing "Kanawana" with "Sir George Williams".

================================================================================
2. Bonnie Buxton and Betty Guernsey, "Montréal Inside Out"
   (Ottawa: Waxwing Productions, 1976)
   Internet Archive item montralinsideo00buxt, scan leaf 296. A city guidebook.

QUERIES: "Kanawana" "Sir George Williams" ; "Kanawana Outing Club, operated by the YMCA near" ;
         "near St-Sauveur, has 20 miles" ; "trips to various trails throughout Quebec" ;
         "of blazed trails, a clubhouse" ; "a clubhouse and babysitting. Instruction and"

RECONSTRUCTED:

  ... [a club that] organizes weekly trips to various trails throughout Quebec. Kanawana Outing
  Club, operated by the YMCA near St-Sauveur, has 20 miles of blazed trails, a clubhouse and
  babysitting. Instruction and rentals available. Phone 849-[...] ...

The phone number is cut off at "849-". The YMCA of Montreal's Drummond Street number in this
period was 849-5331, which is what the 1975 and 1976 national camp directories print for
Kanawana's winter office; the completion is therefore likely but is NOT established here.

The preceding clause belongs to a different club, not to Kanawana, and its name was not
recovered.
